joaquin.nationalityNote: The 2017 Ortega Reunion program describes him among the Filipino candidates for governor and as the first elected Filipino Civil Governor. This is a historical biographical description, not a modern citizenship record.

joaquin.n: Joaquin Ortega y Joaquino was born in Cebu on 11 March 1866 to Antonio Ortega y Verzosa and Juana Joaquino, according to the Ortega Reunion 2017 family-history program. The program says he studied at the University of Santo Tomas and worked with the Compania General de Tabacos de Filipinas (Tabacalera) in Carlatan, San Fernando, in 1889. The Taft Commission appointed him Civil Governor of La Union on 15 August 1901; he became the province’s first elected governor in 1902 and served through 1904. The same family-history account records later public service as Lieutenant Governor in Abra, Bontoc and Mountain Province (1905–1914), assignments involving Lepanto and Benguet (1916–1920), and Special Agent of the Bureau of Non-Christian Tribes (1920–1926). The Provincial Government of La Union confirms his appointment and elected-governor distinction and records that he died on 31 May 1943 at age 77. With Doña Francisca Lacsamana of Bangar, he raised fourteen children. The family program also recalls that he helped move women and children to safety during the American landing at the Tabacalera port, and that he raised his nephew Jesus Ortega Floirendo as his own. These latter details are from the published family account and should be read as family-history testimony, not as independently verified operational or legal records.
joaquin.biographyStatus: Published family-history account and Provincial Government sources; original birth, education, and career records are still desirable.

francisca.n: Doña Francisca Lacsamana, known in the family as ‘Lola Paca’, was born in Bangar, La Union on 9 March 1877 and died on 3 April 1964 at age 87, according to the Ortega Reunion 2017 souvenir program. The Provincial Government of La Union identifies her as the wife of Don Joaquin J. Ortega and confirms that they raised fourteen children. The supplied FamilySearch tree screenshots show Ramona Lopez Lacsamana and Evaristo Guadalupe y Villaverde as her parents; the reunion program independently identifies her brother as Leon Lacsamana. The family program preserves stories of Joaquin travelling from San Fernando to Bangar to court her, and of their Sunday routine of attending Mass. It also describes her home, ‘Daya’, as a welcoming place where relatives arriving from Manila and other distant places could stay and spend vacations, and recalls that she encouraged family gatherings. The name Doña Francisca Lacsamana de Ortega was later given to a memorial municipal high school in Bangar; Batas Pambansa Blg. 458, approved 10 June 1983, converted it into a national high school. The courtship and household anecdotes are family recollections printed in the reunion program; dates and parentage still warrant original civil or parish record corroboration.
francisca.biographyStatus: Dates and family-life account from Ortega Reunion 2017; marriage and fourteen-child family confirmed by Provincial Government; memorial-school name confirmed by Batas Pambansa 458.

leon.name: Don Leon Lacsamana
leon.role: Generation 3 · Son of Ramona and Evaristo · Brother of Doña Francisca · Carlatan
leon.n: Don Leon Lacsamana is identified in the Ortega Reunion 2017 family-history program as the brother of Doña Francisca Lacsamana-Ortega; the reunion publication’s family-tree material also names Leon Lacsamana as Francisca’s brother. The supplied FamilySearch tree screenshots place Leon as a child of Ramona Lopez Lacsamana and Evaristo Guadalupe y Villaverde, but the screenshots are family-tree displays rather than original birth or baptism records. Family-supplied memoirs place Leon in Carlatan, San Fernando, and recall that he walked to visit Francisca and his children at Daya. The reunion program separately describes Daya as Francisca’s open family home for relatives visiting from Manila and other distant places; it does not provide a dated record of Leon’s individual journeys. The current family research reports a first marriage under the spelling Cayetana Munar, while the reunion program’s diagram uses Catalina Munar-Lacsamana; it is not yet established whether these forms identify the same person. Family-supplied records and indexes associate Leon with children Alfredo ‘Pidong’, Joaquin, Francisco and Eduardo, and report Paz Munar Lacsamana as a sibling of Eduardo and Pidong. These relationships remain research leads pending original civil or parish records. No reliable birth date, death date, or exact birthplace for Leon has been established. The honorific ‘Don’ is retained as family usage, not as a verified official title.
leon.biographyStatus: Sibling link supported by published Ortega family-history material; parentage, residence details, spouse-name variants and children remain family-tree or family-supplied leads requiring original records.

A 2024 Interaksyon report identifies Jeff as Manoling’s son and Pacoy’s brother. The Inquirer (November 14, 2018) identifies him as one of the eight Ortega brothers. Poro Point Management Corporation published a condolence notice for him on December 5, 2025, naming his wife Geraldine “Denny” and son Manuel Victor “Mannix”. A Provincial Government of La Union article (August 2, 2018) describes Denny as his wife and mentions their seven children, but does not name all seven; two unidentified child placeholders are retained rather than inventing names.

joy.n: The Philippine Star (October 10, 2024) identifies Joy as a daughter of Manoling, sister of Pacoy, Mannix and Alfred, and aunt of Rafy Ortega-David. No spouse or children are named in the sources consulted for this update.

jeff-ortega.name: Joseph Francisco “Jeff” Ortega
jeff-ortega.role: Son of Manoling and Denny · brother of Pacoy III, Mannix, Joy and Alfred
jeff-ortega.n: PhilSTAR Life (August 31, 2024) identifies Jeff as the son of former Governor Manuel “Manoling” Ortega and as the brother of Francisco Emmanuel “Pacoy” Ortega III. The article does not identify a spouse or children.

manoling-child-6.name: Unidentified child of Manoling and Denny
manoling-child-6.role: Additional child mentioned in a public family reference · name not identified
manoling-child-6.n: The Provincial Government of La Union article dated August 2, 2018 says Geraldine “Denny” Ortega thanked her husband former Governor Manoling Ortega and her seven children. Five are identified by name in the public sources used for this archive; this entry preserves one of the two remaining unnamed children without guessing a name or gender.

manoling-child-7.name: Unidentified child of Manoling and Denny

manoling-child-7.n: The Provincial Government of La Union article dated August 2, 2018 says Geraldine “Denny” Ortega thanked her husband former Governor Manoling Ortega and her seven children. Five are identified by name in the public sources used for this archive; this entry preserves one of the two remaining unnamed children without guessing a name or gender.

emmanuel-victor.name: Emmanuel Victor Ortega
emmanuel-victor.role: Earlier family-tree entry · relationship needs confirmation
emmanuel-victor.n: This name appeared in the earlier archive as a son of Manoling. The public sources consulted for this update name Pacoy, Mannix, Joy, Alfred and Jeff, but do not clarify whether Emmanuel Victor is another person or a name variant of Manuel Victor “Mannix”. It is intentionally kept unlinked until the identity is confirmed.

paolo.name: Francisco Paolo Padua Ortega V
paolo.n: Wikipedia: born April 14, 1984, “the son of Pablo C. Ortega”. Representative of La Union’s 1st district since 2022 and Deputy Speaker of the House since August 2025.

mariquita.name: Mariquita Padua Ortega
mariquita.n: Identified as Pablo Ortega’s wife by the Inquirer’s 2018 report and the Philippine Star’s 2024 election coverage.

luzan.name: Lucia Esperanza “Luzan” Ortega-Valero
luzan.role: Daughter of Pablo and Mariquita · sister of Francisco Paolo Ortega V
luzan.n: The Inquirer’s 2018 report names Luzan as one of Pablo and Mariquita’s children; the City of San Fernando identifies her as Pablo’s daughter.

mario.name: Mario Eduardo “Tot” Campos Ortega
mario.n: Born Feb 3, 1956. Vice Governor 2019–2025, Governor of La Union since June 30, 2025. Wikipedia lists Victor and Bobby Ortega as his brothers, which places him among Pacoy’s sons, and calls Raphaelle Ortega-David his grandniece.

danielle-bianca.name: Danielle Bianca G. Ortega
danielle-bianca.n: The City of San Fernando and recent La Union election coverage identify Danielle Bianca G. Ortega as Mario’s daughter. A spouse or children are not named in the sources used for this archive update.

justo1.name: Justo “Titong” Orros Sr.
justo1.n: Married Manuela first and, after her death, her sister Joaquina — the same man appears in branch 10.

justo2.name: Justo “Titong” Orros Sr.
justo2.n: The same man as in branch 09: he married Joaquina after her sister Manuela died.

justo-jr.name: Justo Ortega Orros Jr.
justo-jr.religion: Roman Catholic (described as devout and a member of the Knights of Columbus)
justo-jr.religionNote: The Ortega Reunion 2017 biography describes him as a devout Catholic and a member of the Knights of Columbus of St. William the Hermit Parish.
justo-jr.n: A former Pangasinan judge, elected Governor of La Union in 1992 and in office 1992–2001 (Ortega Reunion 2017 and other published references). The Inquirer calls him “a cousin of the Ortegas” without naming his parents; he is placed under Joaquina and Justo Sr. as in your draft, so confirm that link.

jay-jay.name: Jay-jay Orros
jay-jay.n: Described as the son of former governor Justo Ortega Orros and a provincial board member (Philstar, 2007).

titing.name: Joaquin “Titing” L. Ortega Jr.
titing.n: Joaquin “Titing” Lacsamana Ortega Jr., born Nov 7, 1916, died Sep 20, 1996. Won the 1969 House race and was elected Governor in 1988 (Wikipedia).

evaristo.name: Evaristo Ortega y Lacsamana
evaristo.religion: Roman Catholic practice documented in family biography
evaristo.religionNote: The Ortega Reunion 2017 biography describes Bisting as modeling faith through attending Sunday Mass.

rosa.name: Rosa Viloria Ubaldo Ortega
rosa.religionNote: The Ortega Reunion 2017 biography states that Rosa became a member of the Secular Carmelite Order (OCDS).

branchNotes.leon: Family-supplied sibling grouping identifies Eduardo, Paz Munar Lacsamana, and Pidong Lacsamana as siblings. Their maternal relationships are not fully established in the supplied information; separate marriage units are retained rather than assuming one mother.
branchNotes.antonia: The reunion biography says they had no children.
branchNotes.vicenta: Carmen later married Jose Protacio Jacinto Jr.; their four sons were Rafael, Jose III, Emiliano and Francisco.
branchNotes.joaquin-jr: The family tree records his death in infancy; no descendants. A later son, Joaquin “Titing” (branch 11), is also styled “Jr.”
branchNotes.jose: Paz is described as a cousin, so this is also a Lacsamana link. Kining and Cleofe had 11 children; Mela and Santos Dacanay had Elena “Ollie”, Pazz “Patchie” and Jose “Third”; Cichit and Emily Alviar had Michelle Ann, Katrina Lyn and Leon Jose “LJ”.
branchNotes.luis: The first five are children of Luis and Lourdes. The reunion biography also identifies Manuel “Padaw” as Luis’s son, raised by Lola Paca.
branchNotes.ramona: Paquita and Froilan Benitez Maglaya had six children. Edward and Maria Victoria “Vicky” Manguerra had six children. Penny and Rolf Kleindienst had a son, John Edward, who died shortly after birth.
branchNotes.juanita: The reunion family-tree diagram names Juanita; the accessible program does not provide a spouse or children.
branchNotes.pacoy: The 2017 reunion biography lists 18 children, including three who died young; the Inquirer (2013) counts 15 — eight sons and seven daughters. Victor, Manuel, Pablo, Mario and other sons are tied to Pacoy by the Inquirer, Wikipedia and Philstar; the governors’ terms come from Wikipedia’s list of La Union governors.
branchNotes.manuela: The reunion biography says Manuela died at childbirth one year after the marriage; no surviving child is listed. Justo Orros Sr. then married her sister Joaquina (branch 10) — the same person.
branchNotes.joaquina: The reunion program identifies Joaquina as Justo Orros Sr.’s second wife after her sister Manuela. Your draft cites FamilySearch for Justo Jr. being their son; that could not be re-checked, and the Inquirer (2013) only calls him “a cousin of the Ortegas”.
branchNotes.titing: Five children are named in the reunion program.
branchNotes.concepcion: The reunion biography says she never married and had no children; she cared for her mother and nieces and nephews.
branchNotes.mary: The reunion biography names three daughters.
branchNotes.evaristo: The reunion biography and the Ortega Twins biography name all six children.
branchNotes.alfredo-pidong: The 1944 register-page scan supports the marriage entry and records Alfredo’s parents as Leon Lacsamana and Cayetana Munar. The five children listed under Alfredo and Juanita come from the family-supplied update; no individual birth records are attached yet.
branchNotes.jerry: Milagros Gandingan is identified as Jerry’s wife in family-supplied notes. Their children are listed from the same update; the youngest daughter remains unnamed as Private.
branchNotes.richard-lee: Ariane Agnes is identified as Richard Lee’s wife in family-supplied notes. Their two daughters are intentionally displayed as Private.

familyIndex.name: Don Leon Lacsamana · La Union
familyIndex.how: Leon is reported as Francisca’s brother. His reported children include Alfredo “Pidong”, Joaquin, Francisco and Eduardo; the scanned contracts identify the parents named in the Joaquin, Francisco and Eduardo entries. Alfredo and Juanita’s five children are listed from the family update. The Eduardo branch continues through Jeffrey, Adrian and Eloisa; Edna, Arthur Lee Jr., Richard and Noel John; and Jerry with wife Milagros and their named / privacy-protected children. Sheryll Dacanay’s parent names are family-supplied leads. Family-supplied relationships remain provisional where original records are not attached.

familyIndex.name: Munar · Garcia
familyIndex.how: Cayetana Munar and Emilia / Emiliana Garcia are listed as Leon’s first and second wives in the supplied family research. The earlier Catalina Munar spelling remains unresolved.

familyIndex.name: Valdris · Valdivia · Bautista
familyIndex.how: Juanita is named “Valdris” in the earlier supplied index and appears as “Valdivia” in the supplied 1944 register-page scan and family biography. The scan lists Andres Valdivia and Marcelina Bautista as her parents. Keep Valdris / Valdivia as an unresolved spelling discrepancy pending a certified copy.

familyIndex.name: Viloria · Nuval
familyIndex.how: The 2 January 1955 marriage contract names Leocadio Viloria and Prisea Nuval as Concepcion’s parents. A separate update note spells the mother’s name “Prinsea”; the scan appears to read “Prisea”.

familyIndex.name: Lomiteng · Buyao
familyIndex.how: The 8 September 1958 marriage contract names Mariano Lomiteng and Rafaela Buyao as Pacita’s parents and records the marriage to Francisco Lacsamana in San Fernando, La Union.

familyIndex.name: Argueza · Rillera
familyIndex.how: The 27 July 1959 marriage contract names Isabelo Argueza and Concepcion Rillera as Purita’s parents. It records Eduardo Lacsamana age 36 years 11 months, which conflicts with the earlier index-based birth-year estimate.

familyIndex.name: Lee · Edna Lacsamana’s descendants
familyIndex.how: Edna Lacsamana and Arthur Lee Jr. are listed as the parents of Richard Lee and Noel John Lee. The family update adds Richard’s wife Ariane Agnes and two daughters whose names are withheld as Private.

familyIndex.name: Separate Leon record groups
familyIndex.how: Separate Leon Lacsamana record groups are retained. The 16 November 1962 marriage contract identifies Macario’s parents as Leon Lacsamana and Alejandra Capalad and Felicidad’s parents as Ramon Santos and Candida Lacsamana. This is not evidence that this Leon is Don Leon of La Union.

familyIndex.name: Ancheta
familyIndex.how: Antonia Ortega married Gov. Pio Ancheta, Governor of La Union 1919–1922. They had no children.

familyIndex.name: Panis · Jacinto
familyIndex.how: Vicenta Ortega married Col. Emiliano Panis, a surgeon and lawyer. Their daughter Carmen later married Jose Protacio Jacinto Jr.; they had four sons.

familyIndex.name: Balingit · Dacanay · Alviar
familyIndex.how: Through the children of Jose Alvaro Ortega and Paz Lacsamana: Kining married Cleofe “Pet” Balingit (11 children), Mela married Santos Dacanay, and Cichit married Emily Alviar.

familyIndex.name: Rivero
familyIndex.how: Luis Ortega married Lourdes Favis Rivero; they had five children, and Luis also had a son, Manuel “Padaw”.

familyIndex.name: Montilla · Maglaya · Manguerra · Kleindienst
familyIndex.how: Ramona Ortega married Col. Eduardo Resurreccion Montilla. Their children married Froilan Benitez Maglaya (Paquita), Maria Victoria “Vicky” Manguerra (Edward) and Rolf Kleindienst (Penny).

familyIndex.name: Campos
familyIndex.how: Francisco “Pacoy” Ortega, congressman, married Corazon Campos of Bauang. Their sons Victor and Mario Eduardo carry Campos as a middle name, and several became governors of La Union.

familyIndex.name: Alviar
familyIndex.how: Vini Nola Alviar married Francisco “Pacoy” Ortega III, Governor 2016–2022; Emily Alviar married Leon “Cichit” Ortega. Whether the two Alviar families are related is not stated.

familyIndex.name: Orros
familyIndex.how: Manuela, and after her death her sister Joaquina, married Justo “Titong” Orros Sr. Justo Orros Jr., a judge and Governor of La Union 1992–2001, is placed as Joaquina’s son following your draft (the Inquirer calls him “a cousin of the Ortegas”); his son Jay-jay served on the provincial board.

familyIndex.name: Nuesa
familyIndex.how: Joaquin “Titing” Ortega, Governor 1988–1992, married Felicula “Fely” Nuesa; they had five children.

familyIndex.name: Gonong · Peralta · Cantorna
familyIndex.how: Maria Ortega married Dr. Fernandico Gonong. Their daughters are Marietta Gonong, Teresita “Tessie” Peralta and Fernandica “Dinah” Cantorna.

familyIndex.name: Ubaldo · Bolong · Argel
familyIndex.how: Evaristo Ortega married Rosa Viloria Ubaldo. Their six children include the twins Ma. Luz “Luchie” Bolong and Ma. Nila “Nile” Argel.

familyIndex.name: Dacanay · Natarte
familyIndex.how: The supplied family update names Rufino Dacanay and Felicidad Natarte as Sheryll Dacanay’s parents. This relationship remains a family-supplied lead; no original birth or civil record has been attached.
